# Hooks reference

The detail behind [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md), loaded only when needed. The tool owns
the tables - `hooktool events` for events, `hooktool fields` for handler fields -
and the official [hooks reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks) owns
each event's input schema; this file keeps the evaluation rules, the protocol and
observed behaviour. **(tested)** marks a statement confirmed by a headless
experiment on 2.1.295. `hooktool` throughout means
`python3 <this skill's directory>/scripts/hooktool.py`: the plugin puts nothing
on PATH, so there is no bare command.

## How a hook fires

When an event fires and a matcher group matches, Claude Code runs every handler
in the group, in parallel. The handler gets a JSON payload - on **stdin** for
`command` hooks, as the **POST body** for `http` hooks - and signals back through
its **exit code** and optionally **stdout JSON**.

The same handler defined in more than one settings file runs once; a plugin's or
skill's copy of it stays separate and runs as well. Hook entries merge across
settings levels rather than replacing each other.

## Events

`hooktool events` prints every event in lifecycle order: whether exit 2 blocks,
which field the matcher filters, whether plain stdout or `additionalContext`
reaches Claude, and the closed matcher values. `events --json` adds, per event,
the handler types it runs and a note on what exit 2 does there - read the note
before relying on stderr from an event that cannot block: it goes to Claude, the
user, the debug log or nowhere, depending on the event.

Two things the table cannot say:

- A handler of a type the event does not run is skipped without an error at run time (`hooktool validate` makes it one).
- On `SessionStart` an `mcp_tool` handler is skipped at launch, before MCP servers connect.

## Matchers

Omit `matcher`, or use `"*"` or `""`, to fire on every occurrence. A matcher on an
event that takes none is silently ignored, and a value outside an event's closed
set never matches (`hooktool events` lists the sets). Otherwise the characters
decide how it is evaluated:

| Matcher | Evaluated as | Example |
|---|---|---|
| only letters, digits, `_`, `-`, spaces, `,`, `\|` | exact string, or a list of exact strings separated by `\|` or `,` | `Bash`; `Edit\|Write`; `code-reviewer` |
| contains anything else | JavaScript regex, **unanchored** | `mcp__memory__.*`; `^Notebook`; `Edit.*` also matches `NotebookEdit` |

Consequences worth knowing:

- `mcp__memory` is an exact string and matches no tool. Write `mcp__memory__.*`. A plugin's own MCP tools are named `mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<tool>`.
- A plugin-scoped agent type such as `my-plugin:reviewer` contains a colon, so it is a regex: anchor it, `^my-plugin:reviewer$`.
- `FileChanged` and `StopFailure` use a narrower exact set (letters, digits, `_`, `|`).
- A `SubagentStop` matcher that names agent types does not match the empty `agent_type` of Claude Code's internal agents; an omitted matcher does.

**Tool names (tested, 2.1.295).** The file-writing tools are `Write`, `Edit` and
`NotebookEdit`. `MultiEdit` is not in the tool list any more; a matcher that
names it is dead weight. `NotebookEdit` carries `tool_input.notebook_path`, not
`file_path`. The subagent tool reports as `Agent`. A `PostToolUse` hook on
`Edit|Write` does not fire when a Bash command rewrites the file - use
....
`CLAUDE_EFFORT` when the model supports effort levels. Plugin hooks also get `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`, `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA`
and `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_<KEY>` per user-config value. `SessionStart`, `Setup`,
`CwdChanged` and `FileChanged` hooks get `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE`: append `export`
lines to it to set variables for later Bash commands. `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE` is
`"true"` in cloud sessions.

`${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}`, `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` and `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` are
also substituted as placeholders in `command` and `args`. Handlers run in the
session's current directory, so reference scripts through a placeholder, never a
relative path.

## Hooks in skills and agents

Hooks can live in a skill's or subagent's `hooks:` frontmatter, in the same
shape as in settings.

- **Skill**: registered when the skill is invoked and kept **for the rest of the session**, not just the skill's turn.
- **Subagent**: active only while that subagent runs. A `Stop` hook there is converted to `SubagentStop`.
- **Plugin subagent**: its hooks go in the plugin's `hooks/hooks.json` with an agent-type matcher, because frontmatter `hooks` is among the fields `claude-lint fields agent` marks as ignored there.

Settings, managed and plugin hooks also fire **inside** subagents for their tool
calls, with `agent_id` and `agent_type` in the payload.

## Hooks in a plugin

A plugin ships hooks in `hooks/hooks.json` at the plugin root, and may add more
through the `hooks` key of `plugin.json` (a path, an inline object, or an array
of either). Both load and merge. They register when the plugin loads - no skill
has to be invoked first - and changes need `/reload-plugins` or a restart.

- **A hooks file needs the outer `{"hooks": {...}}` wrapper.** A file holding only the event map fails to load, with no hook firing and nothing in the transcript (tested). A top-level `description` is allowed. The inline object in `plugin.json` is the event map itself, without a wrapper (tested).
- **Paths go through `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`**, never a hard-coded path; the install path changes across updates and can contain spaces. `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` is the directory for state that survives updates.
- **Quoting.** In shell form wrap the placeholder in double quotes; exec form needs none. With the plugin installed under a directory named `my plug` (tested), `sh "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/x.sh"`, `sh "$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/hooks/x.sh"` and exec-form `sh` + `["${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks

## Matchers

Omit `matcher`, or use `"*"` or `""`, to fire on every occurrence. A matcher on an
event that takes none is silently ignored, and a value outside an event's closed
set never matches (`hooktool events` lists the sets). Otherwise the characters
decide how it is evaluated:

| Matcher | Evaluated as | Example |
|---|---|---|
| only letters, digits, `_`, `-`, spaces, `,`, `\|` | exact string, or a list of exact strings separated by `\|` or `,` | `Bash`; `Edit\|Write`; `code-reviewer` |
| contains anything else | JavaScript regex, **unanchored** | `mcp__memory__.*`; `^Notebook`; `Edit.*` also matches `NotebookEdit` |

Consequences worth knowing:

- `mcp__memory` is an exact string and matches no tool. Write `mcp__memory__.*`. A plugin's own MCP tools are named `mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<tool>`.
- A plugin-scoped agent type such as `my-plugin:reviewer` contains a colon, so it is a regex: anchor it, `^my-plugin:reviewer$`.
- `FileChanged` and `StopFailure` use a narrower exact set (letters, digits, `_`, `|`).
- A `SubagentStop` matcher that names agent types does not match the empty `agent_type` of Claude Code's internal agents; an omitted matcher does.

**Tool names (tested, 2.1.295).** The file-writing tools are `Write`, `Edit` and
`NotebookEdit`. `MultiEdit` is not in the tool list any more; a matcher that
names it is dead weight. `NotebookEdit` carries `tool_input.notebook_path`, not
`file_path`. The subagent tool reports as `Agent`. A `PostToolUse` hook on
`Edit|Write` does not fire when a Bash command rewrites the file - use

## Hooks in skills and agents

Hooks can live in a skill's or subagent's `hooks:` frontmatter, in the same
shape as in settings.

- **Skill**: registered when the skill is invoked and kept **for the rest of the session**, not just the skill's turn.
- **Subagent**: active only while that subagent runs. A `Stop` hook there is converted to `SubagentStop`.
- **Plugin subagent**: its hooks go in the plugin's `hooks/hooks.json` with an agent-type matcher, because frontmatter `hooks` is among the fields `claude-lint fields agent` marks as ignored there.

Settings, managed and plugin hooks also fire **inside** subagents for their tool
calls, with `agent_id` and `agent_type` in the payload.

## Hooks in a plugin

A plugin ships hooks in `hooks/hooks.json` at the plugin root, and may add more
through the `hooks` key of `plugin.json` (a path, an inline object, or an array
of either). Both load and merge. They register when the plugin loads - no skill
has to be invoked first - and changes need `/reload-plugins` or a restart.

- **A hooks file needs the outer `{"hooks": {...}}` wrapper.** A file holding only the event map fails to load, with no hook firing and nothing in the transcript (tested). A top-level `description` is allowed. The inline object in `plugin.json` is the event map itself, without a wrapper (tested).
- **Paths go through `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`**, never a hard-coded path; the install path changes across updates and can contain spaces. `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` is the directory for state that survives updates.
- **Quoting.** In shell form wrap the placeholder in double quotes; exec form needs none. With the plugin installed under a directory named `my plug` (tested), `sh "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/x.sh"`, `sh "$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/hooks/x.sh"` and exec-form `sh` + `["${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/x.sh"]` ran; unquoted `sh ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/x.sh` did not.

```json
{
  "description": "rule on first touch, lint on write",
  "hooks": {
    "SessionStart": [
      { "matcher": "startup|clear|compact",
        "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "sh \"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/reset-rule-delivery.sh\"", "timeout": 10 } ] }
    ],
    "PostToolUse": [
      { "matcher": "Read|Write|Edit",
        "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "sh \"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/lint-on-write.sh\"", "timeout": 30 } ] }
    ]
  }
}
```

The docs now prefer exec form for placeholder paths
(`"command": "sh", "args": ["${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/x.sh"]`). The quoted
shell form above stays correct and is the safer choice for a plugin that may be
loaded by an older Claude Code that does not know `args`.

`${user_config.KEY}` is substituted in exec-form `args` only. A shell-form plugin

cases.prompt: I have a /migrate skill that runs database migrations. While it is running I want a PreToolUse hook that blocks any Bash command touching the production database, but the block should only apply during that skill, not for the rest of my session. Can I put the hook in the skill's frontmatter to get that?

---
```

trajectory.body:
Not quite. A hook in a skill's frontmatter does not end with the skill's run. The reference says a skill's `hooks:` are "registered when the skill is invoked and kept **for the rest of the session**, not just the skill's turn." So a hook declared on `/migrate` would keep blocking production commands after the migration finishes.

Subagent hooks are scoped differently: they are "active only while that subagent runs." That gives you the lifetime you want.

**Option 1 (recommended): run the migration in a subagent that owns the hook.**

Put the hook in a subagent's frontmatter and have `/migrate` delegate its work to that subagent:

```yaml
---
name: migrate-runner
description: Runs database migrations with production writes blocked.
hooks:
  PreToolUse:
    - matcher: Bash
      hooks:
        - type: command
          command: "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/hooks/block-prod-db.sh"
---
```

`block-prod-db.sh` reads the event JSON on stdin, checks `tool_input.command` for production database references, and exits 2 with a reason on stderr when it matches. Exit 0 lets the command through.

I haven't verified whether a skill with `context: fork` picks up the skill's own frontmatter hooks. Delegating explicitly to a subagent is the safer route.

**Option 2: a flag file gated by the skill.**

Keep the hook on the skill, and have the hook script exit 0 unless a marker file exists. `/migrate` creates the marker as its first step and removes it as its last step. The weakness is that the removal is a model step. If the run aborts before it, the marker stays and prod commands remain blocked for the rest of the session. That fails safe, but it is annoying. A timestamp check in the script can expire stale markers.

**Limits either way:** matching on command text is a guardrail, not a boundary. A script that connects to prod, an env var holding the connection string, or a renamed host can get past a string match. If the real requirement is that the migration cannot reach prod, scope the credentials it runs with instead.

I couldn't find `/migrate`'s `SKILL.md` under the working directory, so I haven't edited anything. If you tell me where it lives (for example `~/.claude/skills/migrate/`) and whether you want Option 1 or 2, I'll write the hook script, update the skill, and validate the hook config.

#!/bin/sh
# Stop gate: keep Claude working until `npm test` passes.
# Exit 2 blocks the stop; stderr is fed back to Claude as the reason.
# On Stop, onFailure has no effect, so any exit other than 0 or 2 lets the
# stop through. Every path that does not prove green therefore exits 2.

fi

status=$?

fi

{
  echo "npm test is failing (exit $status). Fix the failing tests before finishing."
  echo "--- last 200 lines of npm test output ---"
  printf '%s\n' "$output" | tail -n 200
} >&2
exit 2

trajectory.body:
The Stop gate is in place: `hooks/hooks.json` registers it, and `hooks/stop-gate.sh` runs `npm test` on each stop. If the tests fail, the stop is blocked and Claude gets the test output as the reason to keep working.

**Blocker: there is no `package.json` in this directory, so `npm test` fails right now.** The gate will therefore block every stop until a `package.json` with a `test` script exists. I did not create one, because a made-up test script would just be a fake pass. Tell me which test runner you want, or add the file yourself, and the gate will start reflecting real results.

**What I verified**
- `hooktool validate hooks/hooks.json` passes with 0 warnings.
- I ran the script directly against scratch projects:
  - passing tests: exit 0, the stop is allowed
  - failing tests: exit 2, with the output in stderr
  - no `package.json`: exit 2
  - `npm` not on PATH: exit 2
  - a missing project directory: exit 2
  - a simulated internal crash: exit 2, via a trap
- I have not run a live Claude Code session. The plugin still needs `/reload-plugins` or a restart before the hook registers.

**Design choices you should know about**
- **Fails closed.** On `Stop`, Claude Code's `onFailure: "block"` has no effect, so the script itself exits 2 on any path that doesn't prove green. A non-zero exit other than 2 would let the stop through.
- **No escape hatch.** The gate ignores `stop_hook_active`, so Claude is sent back on every stop while tests fail. If a test can't be fixed, Claude will keep trying. If you want a bailout, it has to be added deliberately.
- **Timeout is 600 seconds.** A timed-out hook does not block on `Stop`, so a slow `npm test` would fail open. A watch-mode test script would hang and get past the gate.
- **Runs in `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`**, falling back to the current directory.

## Hooks in a plugin

A plugin ships hooks in `hooks/hooks.json` at the plugin root, and may add more
through the `hooks` key of `plugin.json` (a path, an inline object, or an array
of either). Both load and merge. They register when the plugin loads - no skill
has to be invoked first - and changes need `/reload-plugins` or a restart.

- **A hooks file needs the outer `{"hooks": {...}}` wrapper.** A file holding only the event map fails to load, with no hook firing and nothing in the transcript (tested). A top-level `description` is allowed. The inline object in `plugin.json` is the event map itself, without a wrapper (tested).
- **Paths go through `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`**, never a hard-coded path; the install path changes across updates and can contain spaces. `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` is the directory for state that survives updates.
- **Quoting.** In shell form wrap the placeholder in double quotes; exec form needs none. With the plugin installed under a directory named `my plug` (tested), `sh "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/x.sh"`, `sh "$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/hooks/x.sh"` and exec-form `sh` + `["${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/x.sh"]` ran; unquoted `sh ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/x.sh` did not.

```json
{
  "description": "rule on first touch, lint on write",
  "hooks": {
    "SessionStart": [
      { "matcher": "startup|clear|compact",
        "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "sh \"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/reset-rule-delivery.sh\"", "timeout": 10 } ] }
    ],
    "PostToolUse": [
      { "matcher": "Read|Write|Edit",
        "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "sh \"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/lint-on-write.sh\"", "timeout": 30 } ] }
    ]
  }
}
```

The docs now prefer exec form for placeholder paths
(`"command": "sh", "args": ["${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/x.sh"]`). The quoted
shell form above stays correct and is the safer choice for a plugin that may be
loaded by an older Claude Code that does not know `args`.

`${user_config.KEY}` is substituted in exec-form `args` only. A shell-form plugin
INPUT=$(cat)
FILE=$(echo "$INPUT" | jq -r '.tool_input.file_path // empty')
case "$FILE" in
  *.env|*/.git/*) echo "Blocked: $FILE is protected by policy." >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
exit 0
```

Register it with `"onFailure": "block"` if a missing script must not fail open.

**Report linter findings to Claude** (`PostToolUse`, `additionalContext`): the
edit has already happened, so the job is feedback, not blocking. Print the JSON
below on stdout and exit 0 - findings echoed as bare text never reach Claude.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
FILE=$(jq -r '.tool_input.file_path // empty')
[ -n "$FILE" ] || exit 0
FINDINGS=$(ruff check --quiet "$FILE" 2>&1) && exit 0   # clean: say nothing
jq -n --arg ctx "Lint findings for $FILE - fix before continuing:
$FINDINGS" '{hookSpecificOutput: {hookEventName: "PostToolUse", additionalContext: $ctx}}'
exit 0
```

which emits, for example:

```json
{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PostToolUse","additionalContext":"Lint findings for src/app.py - fix before continuing:\nF401 `os` imported but unused"}}
```

**Keep working until tests pass** (`Stop`, exit 2): a handler that runs the suite,
exits 0 to allow stopping when green, or prints a reason to stderr and exits 2 to
push Claude to continue. Guard with `stop_hook_active` so it cannot loop forever
(Claude Code also caps consecutive continuations at 8).

- Hooks guide: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide
- Plugins reference: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference

content:
#!/bin/sh
# Stop gate: Claude may finish only when `npm test` passes.
# Exit 0 lets the stop through. Exit 2 blocks it, and stderr is sent back to Claude.

PROJECT_DIR="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$PWD}"
cd "$PROJECT_DIR" || exit 0

# Nothing to gate on: no package.json, or no "test" script. Allow the stop.
node -e 'process.exit(require("./package.json").scripts?.test ? 0 : 1)' 2>/dev/null || exit 0

OUTPUT=$(npm test 2>&1)
STATUS=$?
[ "$STATUS" -eq 0 ] && exit 0

{
  echo "Stop blocked: npm test failed (exit $STATUS). Fix the failing tests before finishing."
  echo "$OUTPUT" | tail -n 80
} >&2
exit 2

trajectory.body:
The Stop gate is in place. Claude can't finish while `npm test` fails, but there's no test suite in this plugin yet, so right now the gate lets every stop through.

**Files created**
- `hooks/hooks.json`: registers a `Stop` command hook that runs `sh "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/stop-gate.sh"` with a 600-second timeout.
- `hooks/stop-gate.sh`: runs `npm test` in `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`. If it passes, the script exits 0 and the stop goes through. If it fails, the script exits 2 and sends the failure output (last 80 lines) back to Claude as the reason.

**Testing**
- `hooktool validate --plugin` on `hooks/hooks.json` passes with no warnings. `sh -n` passes on the script.
- I ran the script against four throwaway projects in `$TMPDIR`:
  - Failing test script: exit 2, with the failure output on stderr.
  - Passing test script: exit 0.
  - No `package.json`: exit 0.
  - `package.json` with no `test` script: exit 0.
- I did not test the `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` expansion in a live plugin install, and I did not run a real suite.

**Decisions to check**
- **No `stop_hook_active` guard.** The reference suggests one, but it would let Claude stop on the second attempt with tests still red. Claude Code caps consecutive stop-continuations at 8, so after 8 blocked stops in a row Claude will stop anyway.
- **No test script means allow.** Without one, the gate can't block on anything, and blocking would trap Claude in a loop it can't fix. Once you add a `test` script, the gate starts enforcing. If you'd rather block in that case, tell me and I'll change it.
- **Fails open on a crash.** A missing or crashing script doesn't block the stop. Stop hooks ignore `onFailure: "block"`, so I couldn't make it fail closed. An `npm` that isn't installed would show up as a test failure and block.

Nothing is committed. The `hooks/` directory is untracked alongside the rest of the plugin.

I added a Stop hook that blocks Claude from finishing while `npm test` fails. The config validates and the gate behaves correctly against fixture projects. I couldn't run it against your real test suite because this directory has no `package.json`.

**Files**
- `hooks/hooks.json`: registers a `Stop` command hook using `sh "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/stop-gate.sh"`, with a 600s timeout and a status message.
- `hooks/stop-gate.sh` (executable): runs `npm test` in `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`. On failure it exits 2 and sends Claude the exit status plus the last 80 lines of output as its next instruction.

**Verification**
- `hooktool validate hooks/hooks.json --plugin` passes with no warnings.
- Against fixture projects: a passing `npm test` exits 0, a failing one exits 2 with the reason on stderr, and a directory with no `package.json` exits 0.

**Choices you may want to change**
- **No `package.json` lets the stop through.** The gate only applies to Node projects. Blocking here would trap Claude in any non-Node project where the plugin is enabled.
- **A `package.json` with no `test` script blocks.** `npm test` fails with "missing script", so the gate blocks. I left this literal. If you'd rather it pass through, the script needs a check for `scripts.test`.
- **The gate has no escape hatch.** If a test can't be fixed, Claude keeps trying until the tests pass or the hook is removed.
- **Timeouts and crashes fail open.** The validator says `onFailure` has no effect on Stop hooks, so I removed it. A Stop hook that times out or crashes doesn't block. The script itself exits 2 on every failure path it controls, including a failed `cd` and a missing `npm`.
